title: ONLINE-TICS: Internet-Delivered Behavioral Treatment for Patients with Chronic Tic Disorders
newness: Historical 2022 publication newly analyzed on 14 October 2026; not new-window evidence.
design: Five-center observer-blind randomized adult trial; self-directed internet CBIT versus online psychoeducation; face-to-face CBIT available at one center.
population: Ages 18–62 with TS/chronic tic disorders; German/internet eligibility; prior behavioral treatment and comorbidity needing primary therapy excluded; not a defined continuously severe adult cohort.
primary_endpoint: Adjusted YGTSS-TTS change at one week after treatment, iCBIT minus control.
key_result: Primary −1.28 points (95% CI −2.58 to 0.01), p=.053. Later exploratory TTS contrasts favor iCBIT at three/six months; impairment and GTS-QOL have distinct timing. Non-inferiority is exploratory because the prespecified primary gate failed.
uncertainty: MAR-dependent mixed model, differential noncompliance, missing visit/outcome-specific denominators, continued platform access, multiple exploratory tests, and ATQ/impairment table–prose discrepancies.
negative_findings: No clear vocal-tic contrast; video-tic V3/V5 intervals include zero. Early urge and life-satisfaction VAS contrasts point unfavorably under standard scoring; trial VAS recoding unverified. CGI-I responder model failed to converge.
safety: 128 incidents, none investigator-attributed to treatment; event counts differ from affected-participant counts; rare harms remain unestablished.
funding_conflicts: BMBF 01KG1421 and EUR 600 advocacy funding; intervention developers among investigators; multiple financial relationships disclosed in paper.
inference_not_supported: Confirmatory primary efficacy/non-inferiority, endpoint surrogacy, joint response, increasing treatment effect, off-treatment durability, disease modification or cure.
reproducible_analysis: Nine-contrast post hoc Holm/Bonferroni sensitivity retains four of six nominally favorable focal contrasts; 33 checks independently reproduced. Not study-wide or confirmatory adjustment.
retrieval_status: Institutional version-of-record PDF text, protocol and official registry API inspected; screenshots failed. Original summaries/aggregates only saved.
correction_retraction_check: No identified correction/retraction in limited exact-identifier/source check; publisher 429 prevents comprehensive clearance.
next_verification_task: Audit adult-dominant Wilhelm 2012 follow-up estimand, response-conditioned participation and boosters; preserve inclusion of ages 16–17 and stop adult-only inference without subgroup data.

title: Randomized Trial of Behavior Therapy for Adults With Tourette Syndrome
publication_date_type: August 2012 journal issue dated August 1; no earlier online-first date verified
newness: Historical 2012 trial analyzed on 15 October 2026; not new-window evidence. PMC author manuscript available 13 September 2013.
design: Three-site masked-assessor randomized ten-week CBIT versus psychoeducation/supportive therapy (PST); response-conditioned follow-up with offered monthly boosters. PST nonresponders could cross to CBIT.
population: Ages 16–69; adult-dominant, not adult-only. TS/chronic tic disorders with at least moderate severity. Six screened with TTS above 30 received panel review; three enrolled and three excluded. Stable medication/comorbidity and English/IQ criteria limit severe/unstable-adult extrapolation.
primary_endpoint: Week-10 tic severity; categorical CGI-I response (1 or 2) separately reported. Impairment is a registry secondary endpoint.
key_result: Published adjusted acute YGTSS-TTS advantage 3.3 points (95% CI 1.4–5.2), p<.001; impairment advantage 3.9 (0.5–7.2), p=.03 without secondary multiplicity adjustment. Six-month CGI-I positive: CBIT 12/15 assessed versus 12/24 all acute responders; PST 1/2 assessed versus 1/4 acute responders.
uncertainty: Continuous model requires a postrandomization visit and MAR; response-selected and incomplete follow-up, booster-inclusive protocol, unverified actual booster attendance, and control crossover prevent a causal all-randomized six-month comparison. No direct original-report follow-up impairment/GTS-QOL effect or adult-only estimate.
negative_findings: Medication/severity moderator nulls do not establish equivalence. Nine of 24 CBIT acute responders and two of four PST responders have unknown follow-up outcomes.
reporting_discrepancies: Abstract PST 4/63(6.4%) conflicts with body/allocation 4/59(6.8%); six-month prose mixes denominators. Reported NNT5 is not reproduced by reciprocal raw CGI risk difference3.1933 (ceiling4). Author-manuscript and final-published impairment/medication percentages differ.
safety: 224 adverse events and three serious events judged unlikely related; tic worsening in four participants per arm. Event totals differ from affected-person counts; rare or long-term harm not excluded.
funding_conflicts: NIMH and Tourette Syndrome Association support; treatment-manual royalties, professional honoraria and other relationships disclosed; sponsor role declared absent.
inference_not_supported: 80% all-randomized six-month response, continuous remission, adult-only efficacy, off-treatment durability, causal long-term superiority, QoL surrogacy, disease modification or cure.
reproducible_analysis: Exact finite-cohort enumeration gives six-month CBIT acute-responder maintenance bounds 50–87.5%, with 62.5% follow-up ascertainment; not confidence intervals. 37 implementation checks plus 49 independent comparison checks passed; output reproduced exactly.
retrieval_status: Final JAMA HTML, PubMed, current official registry API, one readable PMC manuscript fetch and visually inspected PMC flow diagram. No full papers or figures included in deliverables.
correction_retraction_check: None identified in bounded exact-title/DOI searches and inspected PubMed record; not comprehensive clearance.
next_verification_task: Audit same-trial McGuire secondary functioning report (PMID31451122; online2019-08-27, issue2020-09): randomized acute disability/social/family effects versus responder associations and selected follow-up; retain denominators, instrument direction, uncertainty, multiplicity and null findings.

title: An online survey investigating the experiences of tic-related pain and use of pain management techniques in people with tics and tic disorders
study_type: Cross-sectional, self-selected English-language online survey with descriptive quantitative summaries and inductive thematic analysis.
population: 181 respondents aged 16–71 from 18 countries; eligibility required current tics AND tic-related pain, age≥16, suspected or confirmed tic disorder, and English literacy. Online patient/support/research channels. No adult-only or severe-persistent-adult estimate.
recruitment: Four of eight approached national TS charities advertised; an online TS community, NIHR MindTech social media and circulation to 47 TS support associations. Exposure, starts, exclusions, dropouts, response rate not given.
comparator: No randomized or population control. Separately reported tic- and pain-interference domain means, with matched contributing sets unverified.
exposure: Current self-attributed tic-related pain selected at entry; self-reported pain causes, care and management histories; no assigned intervention.

outcomes.interference: Adapted 13-domain BPI-SF-related scale scored 1–5, previous-week recall, N/A choice; each domain mean/SD reported separately for tics and pain.
outcomes.validation: No validation of expanded adaptation, full question stems, middle labels or clinically important threshold supplied in checked report.
outcomes.tic_severity: Adult Tic Questionnaire total 0–216; paper describes current severity without a separate explicit recall-window specification.
outcomes.resilience: Brief Resilience Scale; not a pain measure.
outcomes.care: Help-seeking, techniques used and perceived impact of tic treatment; bounded recall period not specified.
outcomes.qualitative: Thematic interpretations, not numerical prevalence or validated causal pathways.

numeric_results.reported_mean_gaps: All 13 tic means exceed corresponding pain means; minimum 0.05, maximum 1.12. Signs robust to conservative ordinary-rounding envelopes. Not established paired differences or adult estimates.
numeric_results.help_conflict: 71+46=117 table seekers versus 118 prose;64.6% matches 117/181, while 118/181 rounds 65.2%.71/117 rounds 60.7%;71/118 rounds 60.2%, neither prose 60.1%.No corrected count adopted.
additional_scope_relevant_conflicts: Highest tic mean 3.86 social situations omitted from prose highest-domain list
Sleep tic SD 1.31 table versus 1.21 prose
General doctor/physiotherapy counts 60/42 table versus 61/43 prose

uncertainty: SDs supplied; no relevant confidence intervals, paired covariance, item valid counts or age-stratified summaries. Rounding envelopes are numerical reporting checks, not sampling uncertainty.
negative_findings: Qualitative reports include variable tolerability and mixed perceived usefulness; no uniform benefit
Unchanged or worse pain reported with tic treatment; not causal treatment harms/effects
Authors did not measure quantitative satisfaction/appraisal of professional pain help
No prospective chronology establishing proposed tic–pain feedback cycle
followup: None prospective; one survey time point with recalled experiences.
attrition: Authors assert no missing outcomes, but N/A was permitted and handling/item counts not supplied. Recruitment/dropout flow unavailable.
adverse_events: No systematic comparative safety analysis; subjective treatment-impact reports are not incidence or causal estimates. Singleton treatment cells not republished.
risk_of_bias: Pain-selected self-selection through online support channels
English/internet access and survey-completion selection
Self-reported diagnosis and pain attribution
Mixed ages, including minors
No persistent-severe-adult stratum
Unknown item-specific N/A handling and response denominators
Cross-sectional recall; unassigned heterogeneous treatment histories
Single lead qualitative coder with discussion/refinement by second author; no causal identification
Reporting inconsistencies retained
conflicts_funding: NIHR MindTech Medtech Cooperative and NIHR Nottingham Biomedical Research Centre cofunding; authors declare no relevant commercial/financial relationships.
applicability: Describes pain-related burden within a pain-experiencing mixed-age convenience sample. Cannot establish population pain prevalence, age≥18 interference estimates, or severe-persistent-adult outcomes.
cohort_overlap_status: No overlap with Małek established; distinct setting/time and no pooling. Independent replication not claimed.
claim_supported: Past-week interference was directly assessed separately from tic severity, and pain burden/support concerns deserve distinct measurement. Marginal mean and qualitative individual-priority statements are different estimands.
claim_not_supported: Representative prevalence, chronic pain duration, adult-only effects, paired significance, clinical meaningfulness, causal feedback, treatment efficacy/inefficacy, comparative self-management benefit, durable benefit, disease modification or cure.
retrieval_status: Publisher HTML/PDF and official EuropePMC XML inspected; PDF pages 5–7 visually verified. No public blank questionnaire, adult-only supplement or linked dataset located. EuropePMC flags hasSuppl=N, hasData=N. PubMed/PMC direct HTML browser-check limits.
reviewer: Research assistant, independent source-method review, separate source/arithmetic review; not clinical peer review.
correction_retraction_check: No linked correction/retraction found in publisher,official XML,Crossref or focused DOI searches; bounded finding only.
next_verification_task: Close Taylor audit absent public correction or methodological clarification. Adult descriptives require age ≥18 item valid/N/A counts, handling, means and dispersion; paired comparison additionally matched n and covariance/difference dispersion. Next distinct candidate: Marras et al. 2001 botulinum-toxin randomized crossover trial, PMID 11245710, DOI 10.1212/WNL.56.5.605. Verify whether pain-specific benefit/interference was measured separately from tic outcomes and procedure discomfort; check adult applicability, carryover and missing numerical prerequisites. Stop without pain-effect inference if no compatible endpoint or lawful full methods.
privacy: Original paraphrases and public aggregates only; no individual narratives, quotations, singleton treatment/demographic cells, family data or full-paper copies. No outreach or participant access.

title: The CM-aGPi Network in the Generation of Tics in Tourette Syndrome
design: Observational intracranial physiology substudy within an implanted-device feasibility trial.
population: Selected medically refractory adults; implanted age range 19–32 years.

baseline_severity.measure: YGTSS total including impairment, out of 100
baseline_severity.population: six implanted participants; not the five-person analytic subset

followup: Nine-visit protocol; main methods describe the initial three postoperative months without recording-time stimulation. Therapy starts in month four; actual visit contributions remain unresolved.
attrition: Six completed the initial three-month postoperative visits. One physiology localization exclusion leaves five analyzed; this is an analysis exclusion, not reported dropout. Later visit-level completeness is not established.

adverse_events.paper: The paper reports no severe or adverse events during the initial three-month postoperative window in six participants; do not extend that statement to all nine months.
adverse_events.linked_registry: Separate NCT05371041 results for eight participants report serious events affecting 3/8, other events 8/8 and deaths 0/8 from enrollment through approximately two years after lead implantation, using non-systematic assessment. Occurrence is not causal attribution.

applicability: Selected severe, medically refractory implanted adults; limited generalization beyond this small surgical cohort. No pain/function mechanism or broad adult natural-history inference.
reviewer: AI-assisted primary-source extraction; separate independent source/methods review linked, not formal clinical peer review.
claim_supported: Tic-associated low-frequency activity and connectivity in simultaneously recorded CM/aGPi add a distinct state contrast relative to earlier audited thalamocortical work, with unresolved analysis-window and testing-unit details.
key_result: Tic-associated low-frequency CM/aGPi power and synchrony; CM phase lead reported.
uncertainty: Recording-window and testing-unit ambiguity; small selected sample; no participant-level contrast CI reconstructed.
negative_and_conflicting_evidence: Beta/low-gamma coherence nulls coexist with low-gamma interhemispheric phase findings; broad Discussion phase-null wording conflicts.
related_cohort_ids: NCT02056873: prior measurement comparator, distinct trial
data_access: Author request statement; registry IPD sharing NO; no granted access.
funding_conflicts: NIH funding; investigational devices supplied by Medtronic; article reports no competing interests.
retrieval_status: Publisher full HTML inspected; linked official registry/protocol/SAP inspected; full supplement unavailable.
correction_retraction_check: No notice identified in inspected views and exact-DOI targeted search; bounded check only.
next_verification_task: Reconcile exact trial clinical outcome construct/time origin using aggregate public metadata; physiology unit/window remains unresolved.

title: Responsive deep brain stimulation for the treatment of Tourette syndrome
design: Prospective consecutive implanted-device feasibility cohort; nonrandomized chronic exposure with randomized-order masked video stimulation-state assessment.
population: Selected medication-refractory adults aged at least 21 with severe disabling TS; YGTSS tic score >35/50. Protocol excludes untreated/unstable psychiatric conditions.
comparator: Preoperative longitudinal baseline is separate from primary-outcome-period video device states; no compatible comparative functional estimator established.
intervention: Clinically optimized continuous and responsive centromedian thalamic DBS across evolving hardware.
outcomes: YGTSS recalled tic severity; Modified Rush video current expression; MOS-36 functional health; psychiatric scales.
followup: Article primary outcome approximately six months after initial implants; protocol video conditions on three separate testing days; registry safety 3 years. Actual common exposure/clock not established.
numeric_result: Article reports 4/8 responders; threshold wording alternates points and percent, Discussion >=30% motor reduction. Selected-responder improvement summaries are not all-cohort effects. No new efficacy calculation.
uncertainty: No compatible aggregate MOS-36 paired denominator, mean-change dispersion/CI, exact recall version or state-specific contrast. Nonsignificance after multiplicity does not establish no benefit or equivalence.

adverse_events.main_paper_summary: Infection-related explantation/reimplantation and separate lead repositioning are reported. No shared six-month risk window is verified.

attrition: Registry flow: 10 complete continuous period; 8 start responsive period, 5 complete. Not a functional-outcome denominator or uniform exposure count.
risk_of_bias: Small selected severe-adult surgical sample; nonrandomized chronic treatment; symptom-guided optimization, hardware changes, response selection, uncertain carryover, functional missingness/precision unestablished.
funding_conflicts: Okun2024 acknowledges NIH R01 NR014852 and R01NS096008 and declares no competing interests. Earlier Cagle report has distinct disclosures and is not substituted for this declaration.
applicability: Severe adult burden is directly relevant, but pediatric and broader adult/comorbidity extrapolation is unsupported.
related_cohort_ids: PMID36094652 / DOI10.1001/jamaneurol.2022.2741: earlier overlapping report, not independent replication
claim_supported: Separation of observed tic-state, recalled longitudinal severity and functional estimands; unresolved aggregate functional precision and endpoint provenance.
retrieval_status: Publisher Okun full HTML, official protocol/SAP and supplement accessible; table headings/notes and aggregate statements inspected. Initial PMC route bot-check; Cagle independently checked through indexed primary excerpts, direct JAMA PDF access unconfirmed. No full text retained.
correction_retraction_check: No notice found in bounded exact-DOI search and publisher view; indexed Crossmark current, live Crossmark access failed.
reviewer: AI-assisted extraction with independent methods review; not formal clinical peer review.
next_verification_task: Official historical NCT02056873 outcome/design version provenance audit; no result rows or participant reconstruction.
privacy: No individual rows or case narratives retained or analyzed. Incidental display in search/supplement parser disclosed in report; no raw signals, contact, intervention or data request.
